The laws of physics that govern our universe have left scientists with a lot of questions. But what if there was a simpler way to look at the universe? Triton is no ordinary moon. With an impossibly young surface and active cryovolcanoes, Neptune’s giant moon has baffled scientists for decades. item.title: What Is It Like on the Surface of a Black Hole Planet?
item.author: Astrum
item.content:encoded:
Scientists are searching for missing planets in the most unlikely place. Astrum books are still available in the US! If you’re fascinated by the cosmos, want to learn more about our Solar System, or just love stunning space images, get your hands on an Astrum book here: https://astrumspace.co/
▀▀▀▀▀▀
At the edge of a supermassive black hole lies one of the most violent, hostile environments in the cosmos. It's the last place anyone expected to find a planet, but scientists now believe missing worlds could be lurking here. How do these black hole planets form? What are their surfaces like? And how do we actually find them?

This Astrum supercut is a complete guide to the Milky Way. If we can map galaxies billions of light-years away... why is our own home still such an enigma?

item.title: The Universe May Have Just Revealed the True Nature of Empty Space
item.author: PBS Space Time
item.content:encoded:
Displate’s offering up to up to for 33% off at: https://displate.com/l/spacetime when you use the code: SPACETIME
Nothing is complicated. By which I mean, everything is complicated, because in physics even completely empty space is described as being full of quantum fields doing complicated things even when nothing else is there. So if empty space has these exotic properties, what sort of crazy stuff can we make it do? One prediction that’s been around for a while is that under extreme conditions, empty space can be sort of crystalized. And there’s good evidence that we’ve observed this for the first time.
